title: Hundreds of Global Servers Use AI Hacking Tools, S2W Reports
source_used: SBS News (Korean-language article in English edition); pool item is Chosun Ilbo, which returned no text (0 characters)
key_facts: Security and data intelligence firm S2W released a threat intelligence report on 8 Oct 2026.
According to S2W, hundreds of servers worldwide run the same open-source AI penetration-testing tools used in recent South Korean financial-sector hacks.

Fake sale posts claiming to sell millions of customer records appeared on the dark web and Telegram; S2W found the leak samples it acquired were fraudulently manipulated (overseas emails, rare domestic surnames, legacy phone prefixes).
Financial authorities say account passwords and one-time passwords were not compromised, but loan inquiry history leaked with names and contact details.
Attackers used overseas relay servers, proxies and domestic IPs; most IPs used were not in existing global threat reputation databases.
Critics say most financial companies' security monitoring and CERT staff are outsourced or contract workers.
quote_evidence: According to S2W's analysis, hundreds of servers equipped with the same open-source AI penetration testing tools used in the attacks are currently observed operating worldwide.
Most of the IPs used in the attacks were new addresses not even registered in existing global threat reputation databases (DBs).
why_it_matters_hint: Leaked loan records could fuel targeted voice phishing, and the same AI tools are running on hundreds of servers.
notes: SBS article read in full; SBS notes it was translated by AI and may contain errors. Chosun Ilbo (pool item) returned 200 with no text. Consistent with CrowdStrike's report on the same campaign (C12-02) about the ARTEX tool. S2W is a firm, so the first reporter is the firm; SBS is the outlet credited.
